text: # Incident Report: Phishing SMS Campaign Impersonating NovaTel **Document ID:** INC_C18_INC_2026_0197 **Category:** C18 — Security & Fraud **Department:** Security **Customer Scope:** all **Last Updated:** 2026-05-10 **Version:** 1.0 **Source Authority:** Internal Knowledge Base --- ## Summary A third-party phishing campaign sent SMS messages impersonating NovaTel billing alerts with a malicious link. ## Detection Method Identified during routine NOC dashboard review, ahead of any customer-reported tickets. ## Timeline Flagged via customer fraud reports; anti-fraud short code alert broadcast within 4 hours; domain reported for takedown; law-enforcement liaison initiated. | Time | Event | Observation | Action | |---|---|---|---| | T+0 | Fault detected | Alarm/ticket volume triggers investigation | On-call engineer paged | | T+10m | Initial triage | Affected scope estimated | Field/remote team engaged as needed | | T+Xh | Interim mitigation | Partial service restored where possible | Status page updated | | T+Yh | Full restoration | Service confirmed normal | Incident closed, RCA initiated if required | ## Customer Impact Estimated customers affected and service categories impacted are recorded in the internal incident-management system (ref: INC-2026-0197). Customer-facing status was published under Network > Service Status for the outage duration. ## Initial Hypothesis The initial working theory pointed to the most probable cause based on alarm signatures and affected-scope pattern; this was confirmed or revised during investigation. ## Investigation The response team correlated alarm data, affected-site/customer patterns, and any recent change or third-party activity in the area to isolate the fault to a specific component or cause before
title: Phishing SMS Campaign Impersonating NovaTel
